old: One last request, if I may,
new: If anything happens, I have one request to make,
reason: Source: 'If anything happens, I have one request to make of you'. 'last' is invented and the conditional that opens Porfiry's circling approach ('If anything happens... If anything were to happen') is dropped.

old: Just as a man might endure half an hour of mortal terror with a robber — yet when the knife is finally at his throat, he feels no fear.
new: So a man will sometimes endure half an hour of mortal terror with a robber, yet when the knife is finally at his throat, he feels no fear.
reason: The sentence is a fragment ('Just as...' with no main clause), which is hard to follow when heard. [verifier-modified: The fragment is real. But the proposal invents 'alone' and still loses the source's 'sometimes'. Source: 'So a man will sometimes go through half an hour of mortal terror with a brigand, yet when the knife is at his throat at last, he feels no fear.']

old: There have been Wanderers in his family
new: There have been Wanderers — members of a religious sect — in his family
reason: A listener hears the translator's note only as a detached line afterwards; a short inline gloss tells them who the Wanderers are at the moment it matters.

new: because I'm such a Schiller, such an idealist?
reason: This is the first use of 'Schiller' as shorthand for a romantic idealist, and a listener will not know the allusion. [verifier-modified: A gloss helps, but 'starry-eyed' adds a colouring of the translator's own. The source itself pairs the two words at 34.75 ('You--a Schiller, you--an idealist!'), so reuse that. Also, this is not the first Schiller reference, since 'Schilleresque' appears in Part 1.]

old: in this one is bound to go to excess
new: in this, one is bound to go to excess
reason: Without the comma, 'this one' is misread as a noun phrase.

old: She thought it showed I was unwilling to deceive her by warning her in advance
new: She thought that by warning her in advance I showed I was unwilling to deceive her
reason: The misplaced 'by warning her in advance' makes the sentence hard to follow on first hearing.

new: _la nature et la vérité_ — nature and truth! Ha-ha!
reason: This French phrase is left unglossed, while the others nearby are glossed.
The Molière line is 'Où la vertu va-t-elle se nicher?'; 'O' is a misspelling.
